title: Linear first-order PDEs, characteristic directions, and level curves
section: Chapter 4 Review Questions ▷ First-order partial differential equations
terms: first-order PDE; transport equation; characteristic curve; directional derivative; gradient; level curve.

exposition.text:
For constants a, b, not both zero, the PDE au +bu = 0 says the directional derivative of u along
x y
(a, b) vanishes. Thus u is constant on lines in that direction, the characteristic curves. Locally
the general differentiable solution is u(x, y) = F (bx − ay), since bx − ay is unchanged along each
characteristic.
Initial values along a curve can determine F if the curve crosses the characteristics rather than
following one. The chain rule verifies a proposed solution quickly. More generally, au + bu = c
x y
means u changes linearly at rate c along a parameterized characteristic. Domain geometry can
affect the global form, so local characteristic descriptions need compatible connected regions for
global claims.
′ ′ ′
For variable coefficients, characteristic curves solve x = a(x, y) and y = b(x, y), with u =
c(x, y) along them. They need not be straight lines. A global description by one invariant also
requires consistency across characteristic components: a connected domain can intersect one
characteristic line in separate pieces on which the constants differ.

For u + u = 0 on R , compare the data (I) u(t, t) = t and (II) u(t, t) = 1 for all real t. How
x y
1
many C solutions does each set of data admit?
(A) I: none; II: exactly one
(B) I: none; II: infinitely many
(C) I: exactly one; II: exactly one
(D) I: infinitely many; II: infinitely many
(E) I: exactly one; II: none

solution.text:
The diagonal is a characteristic. Along it, the chain rule gives d[u(t, t)]/dt = u + u = 0, con-
x y
tradicting data I. Data II are compatible but constrain only one characteristic: every u =
F(x − y) with F(0) = 1 works. Characteristic data can be inconsistent or insufficient for
uniqueness.
